evidence: Cic. Planc. 97: eōrum precēs et vōta exaudiēns (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The classical word for prayer to God or the gods, nearly always plural; the singular lives on in the ablative prece (Hor., Ov.). To say one’s prayers is precēs dīcere (Schottennius) or recitāre (Vives).

evidence: Vulg. Act. 1.14: erant persevērantēs ūnanimiter in ōrātiōne
terms.comment: Classically a speech; in the Vulgate and the Church a prayer, and prayer itself (Lewis & Short), as in Ōrātiō Dominica, the Lord’s Prayer.

terms.gloss: a prayer, a set form of prayer
evidence: Cic. Mur. 1: sollemnis comitiōrum precātiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: One prayer or its set words; the school dialogues call the Lord’s Prayer precātiō Dominica (Vives, Corderius; Morgan–Owens).

phrases.latin: grātēs perāctō jam diē et noctis exortū precēs
phrases.english: thanks, now the day is done, and prayers as night comes on

phrases.latin: Porcōrum est edere, nūllīs precibus dictīs.
phrases.english: Eating without saying grace is for pigs.
phrases.source: Schott. Conf., Ante et post cibum hymnum esse dīcendum

phrases.english: and the prayer of faith will save the sick man
